test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 21 March, 2023 Shift 4)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following pairs of 'elements - valency' is correct?

I. Boron - 2

II. Fluorine -3
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fluorine** has a **valency of 1 **because it needs to gain only **one electron** to achieve a** stable electron configuration of 8 valence electrons.**
 
• **Boron** has a** valency of 3** because it tends to lose its** three valence electrons **to achieve a stable electron configuration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Valency,** also known as** oxidation number,** is a **measure of an element's combining capacity** or the** number of electrons it can gain, lose, or share when forming chemical compounds.**
 
• It determines** how an element will bond with other elements to form compounds.**
 
• The valency of an element is determined by the** number of valence electrons it possesses.**
 
• **Valence** electrons are the electrons present in the outermost energy level or shell of an atom.
 
• These electrons are involved in **chemical reactions** and have the potential to participate in** bonding**.
